citing.title: On Higher-performance Sparse Tensor Transposition
citing.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Parallel & Distributed Processing, Workshops and Phd Forum
contexts: We use for evaluation a set of representative 3D tensors collected from the FROSTT Tensor Collection [18], which have been used extensively in similar studies [1], [19], [12].
TACO [12] uses the same implementation as SPLATT, but proposes an algorithm called Top-K-Sadilla, which enables skipping sorting passes on certain dimensions of coordinates based on their priority.

We describe the properties of the seven tensors in Table I. Note that we sort all dimensions of the coordinates just for performance comparison between different approaches, although some dimensions can be skipped, depending on the target permutation [12].

This also provides a uniform way of performing sparse tensor transpose, in which we convert any sparse tensor format to the COO format, perform the transpose, and then convert it back to the input sparse tensor format, which is the common approach adopted by related works [11], [12].
There have been a couple of research works targeting tensor transposition on sparse tensors for performance improvement [11], [12], [9], [20].
We can observe that count sort is the most performant one, which is also aligned with the time complexity of sorting and the previous studies [12].
Mueller et al. [12] designed a strategic approach that allows skipping a couple of dimensions of coordinates while sorting according to the ordering priority.
